$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff 
\mu\bigl[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\bigr]=S_{0}\;,
\tag{2}
$$

the $\sin kx$ mode satisfying $u_{x}=0,\;\sigma_{xz}=0$ on $x=0$,
$L=\lambda/2$.  With $\alpha=kh$ the two conditions (2) give with
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
a_{2}= \frac{S_{0}}{\mu}\,
       \frac{h\cosh\alpha}
            {2\bigl[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}\bigr]},\qquad
\Phi'''(0)=2k^{2}a_{2},
$$

and on the stationary state $\dot e=0$ from (1)

$$
\rho g\,e_{s}= \frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)
           =S_{0}\,\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
                       {\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}
           \equiv S_{0}K(\alpha) ,
$$

i.e. in the $\rho$–formulation

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,K(\alpha),\qquad
K(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
               {\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}
        =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}
              +\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}\Bigg]^{-1},
\qquad\alpha=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda} .
$$

Writing the restoring buoyancy at the free surface as $\Delta\rho g$,
$\rho g\to\Delta\rho g$, the shear induced dynamic topography in
magnitude is

$$
\bigl|e_{s}\bigr|=
\chi_{0}(\alpha)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{0}(\alpha)=K(\alpha)=
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}
 =\Big[\cosh\alpha/\alpha+\alpha/\cosh\alpha\Big]^{-1},
$$

$\alpha=kh$.  With the upward positive convention the $\cos kx$
topography is $180^{\circ}$ out of phase with the imposed
$\sin kx$ basal shear,

$$
e_{s}= -\, \chi_{0}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

the minus sign being the usual crest-trough phase shift.  In
particular

$$
\chi_{0}(\alpha)=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3}),\qquad\alpha\ll1,
$$

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
      \qquad kh\ll1,
$$

the familiar long-wave thin-plate limit, and

$$
\chi_{0}(\alpha)\sim2\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0,\qquad\alpha\to\infty,
$$

with $|\chi_{0}|_{\max}\simeq0.45\!-\!0.50$ at $kh\simeq1.0\!-\!1.2$.

distinct from the net buoyancy,

$$
e_{s}= \frac{\Delta\rho}{\rho}K(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi_{\rm form}= \frac{\Delta\rho}{\rho}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}},
$$

which reduces to $\chi_{0}=K(\alpha)$ for the usual geodynamic
identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$.  Up to the conventional sign
this is the quoted $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with
$\chi(kh)=kh\cosh kh\big/\big[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}\big]$. ∎

1.text:
With the creeping Stokes mode

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi^{\prime}\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,\qquad 
p=P(z)\cos kx ,
$$

${\rm div}\,u=0$ gives $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0,\;D=d/dz$ and
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi^{\prime\prime}+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi^{\prime\prime\prime}-3k^{2}\Phi^{\prime}]
\cos kx$.

and

$$
\Phi(z)=a_{2}z\cosh kz+\big(b_{1}+b_{2}z\big)\sinh kz ,\qquad 
b_{1}=-a_{2}/k ,
$$

$$

      =\rho g\,e(t)\cos kx ,\qquad 
\rho g\,e(t)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi^{\prime\prime\prime}(0) .
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi^{\prime\prime\prime}(h)=3k^{2}\Phi^{\prime}(h),\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff
\mu\!\left[\Phi^{\prime\prime}(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\right]=S_{0},
$$

and the $\sin kx$ mode satisfies $u_{x}=0,\;\sigma_{xz}=0$ on
$x=0,L=\lambda/2$.  With $\alpha=kh$

$$
a_{2}= \frac{S_{0}}{\mu}\,
      \frac{h\cosh\alpha}{2\big[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}\big]},\qquad
\Phi^{\prime\prime\prime}(0)=2k^{2}a_{2},
$$

hence on the stationary state $\dot e=0$

$$
\rho g\,e_{s}= \frac{\mu}{k}\Phi^{\prime\prime\prime}(0)
          =S_{0}\,\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
                       {\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}
          \equiv S_{0}K(\alpha) ,
$$

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}K(\alpha),\qquad 
K(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}
       =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}+\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}
        \Bigg]^{-1}\ge0,\qquad\alpha=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}.
$$

The $\cos kx$ topography is $180^{\circ}$ out of phase with the imposed
$\sin kx$ basal shear, $e_{s}\propto -S_{0}$, i.e. with the upward
positive convention

$$
e_{s}= -K(\alpha)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},
\qquad |e_{s}|=K(\alpha)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},
$$

and the $\sin kx$ mode is the admissible wall mode.  In particular

$$
K(\alpha)=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3}),\;\alpha\ll1,
\qquad 
K(\alpha)\sim2\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0,\;\alpha\gg1,
$$

$$
K_{\max}\simeq0.45\!-\!0.50\;\;{\rm at}\;\;kh\simeq1.0\!-\!1.2,
$$

so that in the long wave thin plate limit

$$
|e_{s}|\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
       =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

the familiar shear induced dynamic topography.  Putting the net
restoring buoyancy at the free surface as $\Delta\rho g$,
$\rho g\to\Delta\rho g$, the conventional geodynamic magnitude is

$$
|e_{s}|=\chi_{0}(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi_{0}(\alpha)=K(\alpha)=
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}
 =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}+\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}\Bigg]^{-1},
\qquad\alpha=kh,
$$

i.e. up to the conventional crest–trough sign

$$

\qquad 
\chi_{0}(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},
$$

which is $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$ and
$|\chi_{0}|\to0$ for $kh\gg1$.  Formally keeping the $\rho$ used in
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ distinct from the buoyancy contrast,

$$
e_{s}= \frac{\Delta\rho}{\rho}K(\alpha)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi_{\rm form}(\alpha)=\frac{\Delta\rho}{\rho}
       \frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}},
$$

which reduces to $\chi_{0}=K$ for the usual geodynamic identification
$\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ and is quoted in magnitude as
$\chi(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha\big/[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}]$, the
minus sign being the $180^{\circ}$ phase shift between the $\sin kx$
basal shear and the $\cos kx$ topography.  With the sign absorbed in
$S_{0}$ this is the quoted $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with
$\chi$ above; $|\chi|_{\max}\approx0.45\!-\!0.50$. ∎

\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}
=\Bigg[\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}+\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}\Bigg]^{-1},
\quad \alpha=kh .
$$

Hence with the usual identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{0}(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
$$

in magnitude, and with the upward–positive convention the $\cos kx$
topography is $180^{\circ}$ out of phase with the imposed $\sin kx$
basal shear,

$$
e_{s}= -\,\chi_{0}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{0}(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}},
$$

the minus sign being the conventional crest/trough phase.  In
particular the long-wave thin plate limit is

$$
e_{s}\simeq -\,kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
   =-\,\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad kh\ll1,
$$

the familiar shear dynamic topography.  Formally keeping the density
$\rho$ in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ distinct from the net buoyancy,

$$
e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}K(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi_{\rm form}(\alpha)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}
       \frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}},
$$

which reduces to $\chi_{0}$ for the conventional $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
identification.  The quoted magnitude is often written simply as
$\chi(\alpha)=K(\alpha)$, up to the conventional sign $e_{s}\to -e_{s}$. ∎
public_text.2:
With the creeping mode

$$
\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx,\qquad u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx,\qquad p=P(z)\cos kx
$$

${\rm div}u=0$, $Re =0$ gives

$$
\bigl(D^{2}-k^{2}\bigr)^{2}\Phi=0,\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\bigl[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\bigr]\sin kx,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}= \frac{\mu}{k}\bigl[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\bigr]\cos kx ,
\qquad D=\frac{d}{dz}.
$$

The regular material top $u_{x}(0)=u_{z}(0)=0$ is 
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ and, up to an additive constant,

$$
\Phi(z)=a_{2}z\cosh kz+\bigl(b_{1}+b_{2}z\bigr)\sinh kz,
\qquad b_{1}=-a_{2}/k ,
$$

so that $\Phi'''(0)=2k^{2}a_{2}$ and

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
            =\rho g\,e(t)\cos kx ,\qquad 
\rho g\,e(t)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0) .
\tag{1}
$$

On $z=h$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff 
\mu\bigl[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\bigr]=S_{0}\;,
\tag{2}
$$

the $\sin kx$ mode satisfying $u_{x}=0,\;\sigma_{xz}=0$ on $x=0$,
$L=\lambda/2$.  With $\alpha=kh$ the two conditions (2) give with
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
a_{2}= \frac{S_{0}}{\mu}\,
       \frac{h\cosh\alpha}
            {2\bigl[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}\bigr]},\qquad
\Phi'''(0)=2k^{2}a_{2},
$$

and on the stationary state $\dot e=0$ from (1)

$$
\rho g\,e_{s}= \frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)
           =S_{0}\,\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
                       {\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}
           \equiv S_{0}K(\alpha) ,
$$

i.e. in the $\rho$–formulation

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,K(\alpha),\qquad
K(\alpha)=\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}
               {\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}
        =\Bigg[\frac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}
              +\frac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}\Bigg]^{-1},
\qquad\alpha=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda} .
$$

Writing the restoring buoyancy at the free surface as $\Delta\rho g$,
$\rho g\to\Delta\rho g$, the shear induced dynamic topography in
magnitude is

$$
\bigl|e_{s}\bigr|=
\chi_{0}(\alpha)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{0}(\alpha)=K(\alpha)=
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}}
 =\Big[\cosh\alpha/\alpha+\alpha/\cosh\alpha\Big]^{-1},
$$

$\alpha=kh$.  With the upward positive convention the $\cos kx$
topography is $180^{\circ}$ out of phase with the imposed
$\sin kx$ basal shear,

$$
e_{s}= -\, \chi_{0}(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

the minus sign being the usual crest-trough phase shift.  In
particular

$$
\chi_{0}(\alpha)=\alpha+O(\alpha^{3}),\qquad\alpha\ll1,
$$

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
      \qquad kh\ll1,
$$

the familiar long-wave thin-plate limit, and

$$
\chi_{0}(\alpha)\sim2\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0,\qquad\alpha\to\infty,
$$

with $|\chi_{0}|_{\max}\simeq0.45\!-\!0.50$ at $kh\simeq1.0\!-\!1.2$.
Formally keeping the density $\rho$ used in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho ge\cos kx$
distinct from the net buoyancy,

$$
e_{s}= \frac{\Delta\rho}{\rho}K(\alpha)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi_{\rm form}= \frac{\Delta\rho}{\rho}\,
\frac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}},
$$

which reduces to $\chi_{0}=K(\alpha)$ for the usual geodynamic
identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$.  Up to the conventional sign
this is the quoted $e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with
$\chi(kh)=kh\cosh kh\big/\big[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}\big]$. ∎

      \frac{h\cosh\alpha}{2\big[\cosh^{2}\alpha+\alpha^{2}\big]},\qquad

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The harmonic Stokes creeping solution is fully converged. With stream function ψ=Φ(z) sin kx, u_x=Φ' sin kx, u_z=-k Φ cos kx, p=P(z) cos kx, div u=0 gives (D²−k²)²Φ=0, D=d/dz. Regular material top u_x(0)=u_z(0)=0 ⇒ Φ(0)=Φ'(0)=0. Up to additive constant

Φ(z)=a₂ z cosh kz + (b₁+b₂ z) sinh kz, b₁=−a₂/k,

Φ'''(0)=2k² a₂,
σ_xz = μ[Φ''+k²Φ] sin kx,
σ_zz = μ k⁻¹[Φ'''−3k²Φ'] cos kx.

Top free-surface condition σ_zz(0)=ρ g e(t) cos kx gives ρ g e = μ k⁻¹ Φ'''(0).

Base z=h: σ_zz(h)=0 ⇔ Φ'''(h)=3k² Φ'(h), σ_xz(h)=S₀ sin kx ⇔ μ[Φ''(h)+k²Φ(h)]=S₀. The sin kx mode satisfies u_x=0, σ_xz=0 on x=0, L=λ/2.

With α=kh the basal conditions give

a₂ = S₀/μ · h cosh α / [2( cosh²α+α² )],

Φ'''(0)=2k² a₂.

On steady state \dot e=0

ρ g e_s = μ k⁻¹ Φ'''(0)= S₀ α cosh α /[cosh²α+α²] ≡ S₀ K(α),

e_s = S₀/(ρ g) K(α), 

K(α)= α cosh α /[cosh²α+α²] = [cosh α/α + α/ cosh α]⁻¹ ≥0, α=kh.

The cos kx topography is 180° out of phase with the imposed sin kx basal shear. With upward positive convention e_s = −K(α) S₀/ρ g, |e_s|=K(α) S₀/ρ g.

Writing the restoring buoyancy as Δρ g, ρ g→Δρ g, the geodynamic magnitude is

|e_s| = χ₀(α) S₀/Δρ g, χ₀(α)=K(α)= α cosh α/[cosh²α+α²].

Formally keeping ρ distinct from Δρ, e_s = (Δρ/ρ)K(α) S₀/Δρ g, i.e. χ_form = (Δρ/ρ) K(α). With the usual identification ρ≡Δρ the factor is unity.

Limits: K(α)=α+O(α³) for α≪1, so |e_s|≈kh S₀/Δρ g =2π h/λ S₀/Δρ g, the familiar long-wave thin plate limit. K(α)∼2α e^{−α}→0 for α→∞. |K|_max≈0.45–0.50 at kh≈1.0–1.2.

All four round-4 derivations reproduce this kernel, differing only cosmetically in sign convention and ρ/Δρ book-keeping. No substantive disagreement remains; the side-wall conditions are satisfied by the sin kx mode. The stable amplitude factor in magnitude is χ(α)=α cosh α/[cosh²α+α²]; signed form e_s=−χ S₀/Δρ g.

4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The Stokes stream-function solution is fully converged. With ψ=Φ(z) sin kx, u_x=Φ′ sin kx, u_z=−kΦ cos kx, p=P(z) cos kx,
(D²−k²)²Φ=0, P=μ k⁻¹[k²Φ′−Φ‴], σ_xz=μ[Φ″+k²Φ] sin kx,
σ_zz=μ k⁻¹[Φ‴−3k²Φ′] cos kx, and with the regular material top u_x(0)=u_z(0)=0 ⇔ Φ(0)=Φ′(0)=0.

Regular branch Φ(z)=a₂ z cosh kz+(b₁+b₂z) sinh kz, b₁=−a₂/k, Φ‴(0)=2k²a₂.
Top normal stress σ_zz(0)=ρ g e cos kx gives ρ g e = μ k⁻¹ Φ‴(0).

Base z=h: σ_zz(h)=0 ⇔ Φ‴(h)=3k²Φ′(h), σ_xz(h)=S₀ sin kx ⇔ μ[Φ″(h)+k²Φ(h)]=S₀.
With α=kh this gives
a₂ = S₀/μ · h coshα / [2(cosh²α+α²)],
ρ g e_s = S₀ α coshα/[cosh²α+α²] ≡ S₀ K(α),
K(α)= α coshα/[cosh²α+α²]= [coshα/α+α/coshα]⁻¹.

Hence in the ρ-formulation e_s = S₀/(ρ g) K(α). The cos kx topography is 180° out of phase with the sin kx basal shear, so with upward positive
e_s = −K(α) S₀/ρ g, |e_s|=K(α)S₀/ρ g.

Writing restoring buoyancy as Δρ g, ρ g→Δρ g, the geodynamic magnitude is
|e_s| = χ₀(α) S₀/Δρ g,
χ₀(α)=K(α)= α coshα/[cosh²α+α²], α=kh=2πh/λ.

Formally keeping ρ distinct from Δρ,
e_s = (ρ/Δρ)K(α) S₀/ρ g = (Δρ/ρ)K(α) S₀/Δρ g,
χ_form = (Δρ/ρ) α coshα/[cosh²α+α²], which reduces to χ₀ for the usual identification ρ≡Δρ. The sign is often absorbed, quoted as e_s = χ S₀/Δρ g with χ>0 in magnitude.

Limits confirmed unanimously:
χ≈α=kh for α≪1, e_s≈ kh S₀/Δρ g;
χ∼2α e^{-α}→0 for α≫1;
|χ|_max≈0.45–0.50 around α∼1.0–1.2.
Side-wall conditions u_x=0, σ_xz=0 on x=0,L=λ/2 are satisfied by the sin kx mode.

All colleagues 1-4 in round 4 give identical kernel K(α). Only notational difference is the conventional crest/trough sign e_s→−e_s and the ρ/Δρ prefactor. No disagreement on ODE, BCs or kernel remains. Unresolved reporting issue is only sign convention; magnitude χ(α)=α coshα/[cosh²α+α²] is settled.

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The harmonic viscous-channel Stokes problem is now unanimously settled across rounds 0-4. With ψ=Φ(z) sin kx, u_x=Φ′ sin kx, u_z= -kΦ cos kx, p=P(z) cos kx,

(D²−k²)²Φ=0,  σ_xz=μ[Φ″+k²Φ] sin kx,  σ_zz=μ/k[Φ‴−3k²Φ′] cos kx.

Regular material top u_x(0)=u_z(0)=0 ⇒ Φ(0)=Φ′(0)=0. Up to constant

Φ(z)=a₂ z cosh kz + (b₁+b₂ z) sinh kz,  b₁=−a₂/k,

Φ‴(0)=2k² a₂.

Basal: σ_zz(h)=0 ⇔ Φ‴(h)=3k²Φ′(h),  σ_xz(h)=S₀ sin kx ⇔ μ[Φ″(h)+k²Φ(h)]=S₀.

With α=kh

a₂= S₀ h cosh α / {2 μ[ cosh²α+α² ]},

Φ‴(0)=2k² a₂.

Top normal stress σ_zz(0)=ρ g e cos kx = μ/k Φ‴(0) cos kx, so steady

ρ g e_s = μ/k Φ‴(0)=2μ k a₂ = S₀ α coshα/[cosh²α+α²] ≡ S₀ K(α).

Hence in ρ-formulation

e_s = S₀/(ρ g) K(α),   K(α)= α coshα/[cosh²α+α²]=[coshα/α+α/ coshα]⁻¹ ≥0,

and |e_s|=K S₀/ρ g. The sin kx mode gives u_x=0, σ_xz=0 on x=0, L=λ/2.

Writing restoring buoyancy as Δρ g, e_s = (Δρ/ρ)K(α) S₀/(Δρ g). With usual geodynamic identification ρ≡Δρ the density factor is set to unity and

e_s = χ₀(α) S₀/Δρ g,   χ₀(α)=K(α)=α coshα/[cosh²α+α²]=[coshα/α+α/ coshα]⁻¹,  α=kh=2πh/λ,

up to conventional 180° phase. With upward positive the cos kx topography is out of phase with imposed sin kx basal shear,

e_s = −χ₀(α) S₀/Δρ g,

minus sign absorbable in sign convention for S₀.

Limits: χ₀≈α+O(α³), α≪1, so |e_s|≈kh S₀/Δρ g =2πh/λ S₀/Δρ g; χ₀∼2α e^{−α}→0, α≫1; |χ₀|_max≈0.45–0.50 around α≈1.0–1.2, |e_s|≈½ S₀/Δρ g for order-unity mode.

All four round-4 contributions reproduce the same a₂, Φ‴(0), K(α) and long-wave limit. Remaining notational difference is only the explicit ρ/Δρ prefactor: formally χ_form=(Δρ/ρ)K, which reduces to χ₀ for the conventional ρ→Δρ identification used in the statement. Sign is conventional. No substantive mathematical disagreement remains; consensus on kernel K and phase shift is complete.

1.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The harmonic Stokes channel solution is now stable.  
Stream function $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$ with $(D^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$. Regular top $u_x(0)=u_z(0)=0$ gives $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ and

$\Phi(z)=a_2z\cosh kz+(b_1+b_2z)\sinh kz$, $b_1=-a_2/k$,

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$.

Top $z=0$: $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ $\Rightarrow$ $\rho g e =\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)$ with $\Phi'''(0)=2k^2a_2$.
Base $z=h$: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\sin kx\iff\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^2\Phi(h)]=S_0$.
With $\alpha=kh$,

$a_2= \dfrac{S_0}{\mu}\dfrac{h\cosh\alpha}{2[\cosh^2\alpha+\alpha^2]}$,

$\rho g e_s=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=S_0\,K(\alpha)$,

$K(\alpha)=\dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\cosh^2\alpha+\alpha^2}
 =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}+\dfrac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}\Big]^{-1}$.

Hence in the $\rho$–formulation

$e_s =\dfrac{S_0}{\rho g}K(\alpha)$, $\alpha=kh=\dfrac{2\pi h}{\lambda}$.

The $\cos kx$ topography is $180^{\circ}$ out of phase with the imposed $\sin kx$ basal shear; with upward positive convention $e_s=-K S_0/\rho g$, magnitude $|e_s|=K S_0/\rho g$.

Asymptotics:
$K(\alpha)=\alpha+O(\alpha^3)$, $\alpha\ll1$;
$K(\alpha)\sim2\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$, $\alpha\gg1$;
$|K|_{\max}\simeq0.45\!-\!0.50$ at $kh\simeq1.0\!-\!1.2$.
Long-wave thin-plate limit $|e_s|\simeq kh\,S_0/\rho g$.

Writing the restoring buoyancy at the free surface as $\Delta\rho g$,
$e_s=S_0K/(\rho g)=(\Delta\rho/\rho)K\,S_0/(\Delta\rho g)$.

$\chi_{\rm form}=(\Delta\rho/\rho)K(\alpha)$.
With the usual geodynamic identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$, $\rho/\Delta\rho\to1$,
$|e_s|=\chi_0 S_0/\Delta\rho g$, $\chi_0(\alpha)=K(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\cosh^2\alpha+\alpha^2]$, i.e. up to sign
$e_s=-\chi_0(kh)S_0/\Delta\rho g$, $e_s\simeq -kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$.

All four colleagues reproduce $K(\alpha)$ and the same $\Phi$, $b_1=-a_2/k$, $\Phi'''(0)=2k^2a_2$, the long-wave limit $kh$ and the maximum $\approx0.5$. The $u_x=0,\;\sigma_{xz}=0$ side-wall condition is satisfied by the $\sin kx$ mode on $x=0,L=\lambda/2$.
The only remaining notational difference is the $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ prefactor; the algebra gives $\chi=(\Delta\rho/\rho)K$, which reduces to $\chi=K$ when $\rho$ is identified with the net buoyancy $\Delta\rho$, as used in rounds 1-4. Sign convention is $e_s\propto -S_0$, magnitude above. ∎

The harmonic Stokes channel solution is now stable.  
Stream function $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$ with $(D^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$. Regular top $u_x(0)=u_z(0)=0$ gives $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ and

$\Phi(z)=a_2z\cosh kz+(b_1+b_2z)\sinh kz$, $b_1=-a_2/k$,

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$, 
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$.

Top $z=0$: $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ $\Rightarrow$ $\rho g e =\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)$ with $\Phi'''(0)=2k^2a_2$.
Base $z=h$: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\sin kx\iff\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^2\Phi(h)]=S_0$.
With $\alpha=kh$,

$a_2= \dfrac{S_0}{\mu}\dfrac{h\cosh\alpha}{2[\cosh^2\alpha+\alpha^2]}$,

$\rho g e_s=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=S_0\,K(\alpha)$,

$K(\alpha)=\dfrac{\alpha\cosh\alpha}{\cosh^2\alpha+\alpha^2}
 =\Big[\dfrac{\cosh\alpha}{\alpha}+\dfrac{\alpha}{\cosh\alpha}\Big]^{-1}$.

Hence in the $\rho$–formulation

$e_s =\dfrac{S_0}{\rho g}K(\alpha)$, $\alpha=kh=\dfrac{2\pi h}{\lambda}$.

The $\cos kx$ topography is $180^{\circ}$ out of phase with the imposed $\sin kx$ basal shear; with upward positive convention $e_s=-K S_0/\rho g$, magnitude $|e_s|=K S_0/\rho g$.

Asymptotics:
$K(\alpha)=\alpha+O(\alpha^3)$, $\alpha\ll1$;
$K(\alpha)\sim2\alpha e^{-\alpha}\to0$, $\alpha\gg1$;
$|K|_{\max}\simeq0.45\!-\!0.50$ at $kh\simeq1.0\!-\!1.2$.
Long-wave thin-plate limit $|e_s|\simeq kh\,S_0/\rho g$.

Writing the restoring buoyancy at the free surface as $\Delta\rho g$,
$e_s=S_0K/(\rho g)=(\Delta\rho/\rho)K\,S_0/(\Delta\rho g)$.
Formally $e_s=\chi_{\rm form}S_0/(\Delta\rho g)$ with
$\chi_{\rm form}=(\Delta\rho/\rho)K(\alpha)$.
With the usual geodynamic identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$, $\rho/\Delta\rho\to1$,
$|e_s|=\chi_0 S_0/\Delta\rho g$, $\chi_0(\alpha)=K(\alpha)=\alpha\cosh\alpha/[\cosh^2\alpha+\alpha^2]$, i.e. up to sign
$e_s=-\chi_0(kh)S_0/\Delta\rho g$, $e_s\simeq -kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$.

All four colleagues reproduce $K(\alpha)$ and the same $\Phi$, $b_1=-a_2/k$, $\Phi'''(0)=2k^2a_2$, the long-wave limit $kh$ and the maximum $\approx0.5$. The $u_x=0,\;\sigma_{xz}=0$ side-wall condition is satisfied by the $\sin kx$ mode on $x=0,L=\lambda/2$.
The only remaining notational difference is the $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ prefactor; the algebra gives $\chi=(\Delta\rho/\rho)K$, which reduces to $\chi=K$ when $\rho$ is identified with the net buoyancy $\Delta\rho$, as used in rounds 1-4. Sign convention is $e_s\propto -S_0$, magnitude above. ∎
